title: Multi-runtime SDK requirements: graceful degradation, streaming contracts, cursor pagination & retry semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD to define cross-language SDK behavior for Python/TypeScript/Go focusing on: robust streaming contracts, cursor-first pagination semantics, explicit retry behavior and graceful degradation when models or regions are unavailable. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, scope boundaries and the rollout plan for the shipping work across SDK owners.
background: Multiple customer reports and internal benchmarks show subtle differences between SDK language bindings when encountering throttling, partial stream failures, or cursor-based pagination migrations. We need a single product-level agreement so apps receive consistent semantics across runtimes and we can safely apply server-side fallbacks and canary rollouts without surprising clients.
requirements: Provide a documented streaming contract for text/chat/embeddings that is implementable in Python, TS and Go (HTTP chunked + optional SSE wrapper).
Streaming API must surface structured chunk types: data, progress/metrics, partial_error, final_status. Each chunk includes monotonic sequence_id and optional resume_token.
Pagination default is cursor-first (opaque cursor object) with an optional server-provided offset for backwards compatibility; SDKs must expose both but prefer cursor helpers.
Retry policy: idempotency keys for mutation-like endpoints, exponential backoff with jitter, explicit non-retriable error classes (4xx), and transparent 429 handling with retry-after respect.
Graceful degradation: SDKs should surface a consistent fallback event when a primary model/region is unavailable and an automatic fallback is performed server-side (e.g., FALLBACK_NOTICE event).
Compatibility: maintain backwards-compatible surface for current v1 contract for at least one major release; provide migration helper functions.
Observability: SDKs must emit standardized client-side metrics and logs for streaming interruptions, retry counts, and final outcome (success/fallback/failure).
Test harness: language-neutral conformance tests and recorded fixtures to be run in CI for each SDK.
acceptance_criteria: Conformance test suite (canonical fixtures) runs in CI for Python/TS/Go with pass rate >= 95% for streaming scenarios.
SDKs implement streaming chunk parser that emits typed events for data/progress/partial_error/final_status and expose resume_token when present.
Pagination helpers and examples added to docs for cursor-first flows and a migration guide from offset-based pagination.
Retry policy implemented in SDKs with configurable max_attempts, backoff parameters and honor for Retry-After header; default settings match product policy.
Graceful degradation surfaced as deterministic event type FALLBACK_NOTICE and documented migration behavior; e2e test simulates primary-region failure and validates FALLBACK_NOTICE emission.
SDK release notes include explicit breaking changes (if any) and a 2-release deprecation window where deprecated functions warn but remain present.
Security sign-off obtained (security_review_required = true) and FIPS/KMS considerations documented for Private deployments.
scope_included: Definitions and shared contract for streaming across all SDKs (parser, event types, resume_token semantics).
Cursor-first pagination helpers and migration docs.
Standardized retry policy implementation and defaults in each SDK.
Conformance test harness and CI integration.
Public docs, examples, and migration guides.
scope_excluded: Server-side implementation of resumable chunk stores — this is an infra/ENG effort (dependency ENG-3124).
Full offline resumable streaming for air-gapped on-prem beyond providing resume_token semantics.
Language bindings beyond Python/TS/Go for this iteration.
compatibility_notes: We adopt a conservative compatibility policy: existing public SDK methods remain stable for at least one major release. When surface changes are required, we provide a dual-path: (1) deprecated method that emits a one-time warning and (2) a new method with the improved contract. Migration helpers will exist in all three SDKs. Backwards compatibility for pagination: if caller sends an integer offset we convert server-side to cursor where possible and return the new cursor to the client in responses.
streaming_contract: Chunk envelope: {type: string, sequence_id: integer, payload: object, resume_token?: string}. (The JSON above is illustrative; SDKs must expose typed events, not raw JSON).
Chunk types: 'data' (partial payload), 'progress' (percentage, latency metrics), 'partial_error' (recoverable), 'final_status' (terminal success/failure/fallback).
Resume_token is optional; when present it is opaque to clients and may be used to request a resumed stream endpoint. SDKs should expose a resume() helper that uses resume_token.
Streaming transports: support HTTP chunked transfer and optional SSE wrapper for browsers; gRPC streams are allowed for internal/private SDKs but public bindings must work over standard HTTP/REST.
pagination_spec: Primary model: opaque cursor string returned in list responses (cursor contains server-side state).
Cursor-first helpers: SDKs provide next_cursor() and iterate_all() helpers that abstract paging loops, batching and rate limits.
Compatibility: accept legacy 'offset' and 'limit' parameters; server returns a compatible cursor on first response to move callers to cursor model.
Edge case: page_size changes (client-supplied) must not break consistency; SDKs should retry read operations when encountering transient EOFs during pagination.
retry_policy: Default: exponential backoff with base=200ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=5s, max_attempts=5 (configurable).
Retryable errors: 5xx, 429 (respect Retry-After), network-level transient failures (connection reset, timeouts).
Non-retryable errors: client 4xx except 429 and 409 (conditional; 409 only retryable if idempotency expected).
Idempotency: for non-idempotent endpoints SDKs must accept an idempotency_key parameter and include it in the request headers. If provided, server-level retries are allowed.

Streaming retries: for short-lived interruptions (<3s) SDKs should attempt transparent resume using resume_token when available. For longer interruptions, emit a partial_error event and surface the need for manual retry.
deprecation_policy: Breaking changes require 2 release deprecation window (minimum) with clear migration docs.
SDKs will emit runtime warnings for deprecated calls and include codemods where feasible in TS.
Critical bugfixes may require patch releases during deprecation window — document any behavior changes in the changelog.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): release SDK changes to beta channel and run conformance tests against canary server. Track error telemetry and metric diffs for 72 hours.
Phase 2 (staged): enable new defaults for 25% of traffic with server-side rollout and opt-out header for customers. Monitor fallback and retry metrics.
Phase 3 (general): flip defaults for all new SDK releases after 2 weeks of stable metrics and publish migration docs.
Fallback: automatic server-side fallback to a compatible model variant must emit FALLBACK_NOTICE event to clients.
open_questions: Should resume_token be usable across SDK versions or strictly server-version tied? (security and privacy trade-offs).
Do we expose low-level raw chunks in TS for advanced consumers or only typed event callbacks?
What is the interaction between SDK-side batching and server-side continuous batching for latency-sensitive workloads?
For private on-prem deployments, do we require a config knob to disable automatic fallbacks?

DX: add examples and migration guide to docs.redwood.ai/sdks/pagination-and-streaming (owner: Marco Silva).
QA: add conformance tests and integrate into CI pipelines (owner: QA Team, ticket QA-789).
Security: run security checklist and confirm compliance for private deployments (owner: Security Team).
notes: Decision: prefer cursor-first pagination to reduce server-side statefulness tied to offsets and to enable more efficient continuation tokens.
Trade-off: opaque resume_token simplifies server evolution but makes debugging harder; we will provide tooling to decode tokens in internal builds only.
Implementation note: TS SDK will default to SSE wrapper in browser environments where chunked transfer is unreliable.
